بازمی‌گردد: پسر، بال‌ها، شیرجه ناخواسته.  

پس این یکی از راه‌هایی است که اسطوره کلاسیک می‌تواند عمل کند: موضوع عینی اشعار، نقاشی‌ها، اپراها و رمان‌ها. اسطوره چه کار دیگری می‌تواند بکند؟  

اینجا فکری هست. فرض کنید می‌خواستید شعری حماسی درباره جامعه‌ای از ماهیگیران فقیر در کارائیب بنویسید. اگر این جایی بود که از آن آمده بودید و این مردم را مثل خانواده خود می‌شناختید، می‌خواستید حسادت‌ها، کینه‌ها، ماجراجویی و خطر را به تصویر بکشید، و همچنین شأن و زندگیشان را به گونه‌ای ثبت کنید که همه آنچه از دید گردشگران و صاحبان ملک سفیدپوست پنهان مانده را منتقل کند. می‌توانستید، گمان می‌کنم، سعی کنید بسیار بسیار جدی باشید، شخصیت‌ها را بسیار جدی و متین به تصویر بکشید، و با فضیلت نیک‌خواهی‌شان آنها را نجیب جلوه دهید. اما شرط می‌بندم که جواب نمی‌داد. آنچه در نهایت به دست می‌آوردید احتمالاً بسیار خشک و تصنعی می‌شد، و تصنع هرگز نجیب نیست. گذشته از این، این مردم قدیس نیستند. آنها اشتباهات زیادی مرتکب می‌شوند: خرده‌بین، حسود، شهوت‌پرست، گاه طمعکار و همچنین شجاع، ظریف، قدرتمند، آگاه و ژرف‌نگر هستند. و شما در نهایت نجابت می‌خواهید، نه تونتو – هیچ رنجر تنهایی اینجا نیست. به‌آن‌ترتیب، ممکن است سعی کنید داستانشان را بر روی داستان کهن‌تری از رقابت و خشونت پیوند بزنید، داستانی که حتی پیروز در نهایت محکوم به نابودی است، داستانی که در آن، علیرغم کاستی‌های گاه شخصی، شخصیت‌ها نجابتی بی‌چون‌و‌چرا دارند. می‌توانید به شخصیت‌هایتان نام‌هایی مانند هلن، فیلوکتتس، هکتور و آشیل بدهید. حداقل این کاری است که برنده نوبل، دریک والکات، در «اومروس» (۱۹۹۰) خود انجام می‌دهد. این نام‌ها، البته، از ایلیاد گرفته شده‌اند، هرچند والکات از عناصر – هم‌نشینی‌ها، اشخاص و موقعیت‌های – هر دو آن و ادیسه در حماسه خود استفاده می‌کند.  

سؤالی که ناگزیر خواهیم پرسید این است: چرا؟  

چرا کسی در اواخر سده بیستم باید به داستانی رجوع کند که به صورت شفاهی از سده دوازدهم تا هشتم پیش از میلاد منتقل شده و شاید تا دویست یا سیصد سال بعد مکتوب نشده است؟ چرا کسی باید سعی کند ماهیگیران مدرن را با این قهرمانان افسانه‌ای مقایسه کند، که بسیاری از آنها از نسل خدایان بودند؟ خوب، برای شروع، قهرمانان افسانه‌ای هومر کشاورز و ماهیگیر بودند. گذشته از این، مگر نه اینکه همه ما از نسل خدایانیم؟ والکات با این هم‌نشینی به ما یادآوری می‌کند که پتانسیل عظمت در همه ما وجود دارد، صرف‌نظر از اینکه شرایط دنیوی‌ چقدر فروتنانه باشد.  

این یک پاسخ است. پاسخ دیگر این است که موقعیت‌ها بیش از آنچه انتظار داریم با هم مطابقت دارند. طرح ایلیاد چندان الهی یا جهانی نیست. کسانی که هرگز آن را نخوانده‌اند به اشتباه گمان می‌برند که داستان جنگ تروا است. نیست. داستان یک کنش واحد و نسبتاً طولانی است: خشم آشیل (فقط پنجاه‌و‌سه روز از ده سال). آشیل بر رهبرش، آگاممنون، خشم می‌گیرد، پشتیبانی خود را از یونانیان پس می‌گیرد، و تنها زمانی به نبرد بازمی‌گردد که پیامدهای عملش بهترین دوستش، پاتروکلوس، را نابود کرده است. در این نقطه خشم خود را متوجه تروایی‌ها و به‌ویژه بزرگترین قهرمانشان، هکتور، می‌کند که در نهایت او را می‌کشد. دلیل چنین خشم‌اش؟ آگاممنون غنیمت جنگی‌اش را گرفته است. پیش‌پاافتاده؟ بدتر می‌شود. غنیمت یک زن است. آگاممنون، که به دستور الهی و احساسات عمومی مجبور به بازگرداندن معشوقه‌اش به پدرش می‌شود، علیه کسی که آشکارترین مخالفت را با او کرده بود، آشیل، با گرفتن معشوقه‌اش، بریسئیس، تلافی می‌کند. به اندازه کافی خرده‌بینانه است؟ نجیبانه است؟ هیچ هلنی، هیچ داوری پاریس، هیچ اسب تروا. در هسته خود، داستان مردی است که به خاطر مصادره عروس جنگی دزدیده‌شده‌اش خشمگین می‌شود، که در پس‌ای از کشتار گسترده اجرا می‌شود، که کل آن به این دلیل رخ می‌دهد که مرد دیگری، منلائوس (برادر آگاممنون)، همسرش توسط پاریس، برادر ناتنی هکتور، دزدیده شده است. اینگونه است که هکتور ناگزیر می‌شود امیدهای نجات کل تروا را بر دوش بکشد.  

و با این حال به نحوی، در طول سده‌ها، این داستان که با دزدی دو زن تسخیر شده، به تجسم ایده‌آل‌های قهرمانی و وفاداری، فداکاری و ازدست‌دادن بدل شده است. هکتور در کار محکوم‌به‌شکستش سرسختانه‌تر از هر کسی که دیده‌اید قهرمان است. اندوه آشیل بر ازدست‌دادن دوست محبوبش واقعاً دل‌اشک‌بار است. دوئل‌های بزرگ – بین هکتور و آژاکس، بین دیومدس و پاریس، بین هکتور و پاتروکلوس، بین هکتور و آشیل – به‌راستی هیجان‌انگیز و پرتعلیق هستند، و پیامدهایشان منبعی از جشن‌و‌شادی و ناامیدی بزرگ. جای شگفتی نیست که بسیاری از نویسندگان مدرن اغلب از هومر وام گرفته‌اند و از او تقلید کرده‌اند.  

و این چه زمانی آغاز شد؟  

تقریباً بلافاصله. ویرژیل، که در ۱۹ پیش از میلاد درگذشت، آینیاس خود را بر اساس قهرمانان هومری الگوبرداری کرد. اگر آشیل کاری کرد یا اودیسه جایی رفت، آینیاس هم می‌کند. چرا؟ این کاری است که قهرمانان می‌کنند. آینیاس به جهان اموات می‌رود. چرا؟ اودیسه رفت. او در نبرد اوج نهایی غولی از اردوگاه دشمن را می‌کشد. چرا؟ آشیل این کار را کرد. و الی آخر. کل ماجرا کمتر از آنچه به نظر می‌رسد اقتباسی است و خالی از طنز و کنایه نیست. آینیاس و پیروانش بازماندگان تروا هستند، پس در اینجا این قهرمان تروایی داریم که الگوهای تعیین‌شده توسط دشمنانش را اجرا می‌کند. افزون بر این، وقتی این تروایی‌ها از کنار ایتاکا، خانه اودیسه، می‌گذرند، به عامل نابودی‌شان ناسزا می‌گویند و لعن‌ش می‌کنند. اما به‌طور کلی، ویرژیل او را به این کنش‌ها وامیدارد زیرا هومر پیش‌تر تعریف کرده بود که قهرمان بودن چه معنایی دارد.  

بازگردیم به والکات. تقریباً دقیقاً دو هزار سال پس از ویرژیل، والکات قهرمانانش را به انجام کنش‌هایی واداشته که می‌توانیم به عنوان بازاجرایی نمادین کنش‌های هومر تشخیص دهیم. گاه کمی کشش دارد، چون نمی‌توانیم دوئل‌های زیادی در میدان نبرد در قایق‌های ماهیگیری داشته باشیم. و نه می‌تواند هلنش را «چهره‌ای که هزار قایق پارویی را به آب انداخت» بنامد. آن عبارت شکوه ندارد. اما آنچه می‌تواند بکند، قرار دادن آنها در موقعیت‌هایی است که نجابت و شجاعت‌ محک می‌خورد، در حالی که به ما یادآوری می‌کند که آنها برخی از بنیادی‌ترین و اصیل‌ترین الگوهای شناخته‌شده برای انسان را اجرا می‌کنند، دقیقاً همانطور که هومر قرن‌ها پیش انجام داد. نیاز به محافظت از خانواده: هکتور. نیاز به حفظ شأن: آشیل. عزم به وفادار ماندن و وفاداری داشتن: پنلوپه. تلاش برای بازگشت به خانه: اودیسه. هومر چهار مبارزه بزرگ انسان را به ما می‌دهد: با طبیعت، با امر الوهی، با دیگر انسان‌ها و با خودمان. در نهایت، چه چیزی وجود دارد که نیاز داشته باشیم خود را در برابر آن ثابت کنیم جز این چهار چیز؟  

البته در جهان مدرن ما، هم‌نشینی‌ها ممکن است آیرونایز (ironized) شوند، یعنی برای مقاصد کنایه‌ای وارونه شوند. چند نفر از ما کمدی سه زند فراری را موازی با سرگردانی‌های اودیسه می‌بینیم؟ با این حال، این همان چیزی است که برادران جوئل و ایتان کوئن در فیلم ۲۰۰۰ خود «ای برادر، کجایی؟» به ما ارائه می‌دهند. این درباره تلاش برای رسیدن به خانه است، نیست؟ یا این، مشهورترین مثال: یک روز واحد در دوبلین در سال ۱۹۰۴، که در آن مردی جوان درباره آینده‌اش تصمیم می‌گیرد و مردی مسن‌تر در شهر سرگردان است، و در نهایت سحرگاه روز بعد به خانه نزد همسرش بازمی‌گردد. کتاب تنها یک سرنخ آشکار دارد که همه اینها ممکن است ربطی به هومر داشته باشد، عنوان تک‌واژه‌اش: اولیس (۱۹۲۲). همانطور که اکنون می‌دانیم، جیمز جویس هر یک از هجده اپیزود رمان را موازی با حادثه‌ای یا موقعیتی در ادیسه تصور کرد. برای مثال، اپیزودی در دفتر روزنامه وجود دارد که موازی با دیدار اودیسه از آیولوس، خدای بادهاست، اما این هم‌نشینی ممکن است بسیار سست به نظر برسد. مسلماً، روزنامه‌نگاران گروهی پرگو هستند و در این اپیزود جلوه‌های بلاغی زیادی وجود دارد، گذشته از این واقعیت که نسیمی در یک نقطه با سرعت می‌وزد. با این حال، تنها در صورتی می‌توانیم آن را شبیه به اصل هومری ببینیم که این شباهت را در آینه‌های کج‌و‌معوج خانه‌های سرگرمی بفهمیم، پر از تحریف و هم‌نشینی‌های مسخره – به عبارت دیگر، اگر آن را به عنوان هم‌نشینی کنایه‌ای بفهمیم. این واقعیت که کنایه‌ای است، هم‌نشینی – و اپیزود آیولوس – را چنین لذت‌بخش می‌کند. جویس کمتر از والکات علاقه‌مند است که به شخصیت‌�هایش نجابت کلاسیک ببخشد، هرچند در نهایت آنها چیزی از آن کیفیت را به خود می‌گیرند. پس از تماشای لئوپولد بلومِ بی‌چاره که تمام روز و نیمی از شب در دوبلین پرسه می‌زند، با بی‌پایان دردسر مواجه می‌شود و اندوه‌های بزرگ زندگی‌اش را به یاد می‌آورد، به خوبی ممکن است احساس کنیم که او به شیوه خود نجیب است. اما نجابت او، نجابت اودیسه نیست.  

اسطوره یونانی و رومی، البته، فراتر از هومر است. دگردیسی‌های «دگردیسی‌ها» اثر اووید در انواع آثار بعدی ظاهر می‌شوند، به‌ویژه در داستان فرانتس کافکا درباره مردی که یک صبح بیدار می‌شود و می‌بیند به سوسک غول‌پیکری تبدیل شده است. او آن را «مسخ» نامید. ایندیانا جونز ممکن است کاملاً هالیوودی به نظر برسد، اما جستجوگر بی‌باک گنج‌های افسانه‌ای به آپولونیوس و «آرگوناتیکا»، داستان جیسون و آرگونات‌ها، بازمی‌گردد. چیزی کمی خودمانی‌تر؟ نمایش‌های سوفوکل درباره ادیپ و خاندان محکوم‌به‌نابودی‌اش بارها و بارها در انواع واریاسیون‌ها ظاهر می‌شوند. در واقع، هیچ شکلی از خانواده ناکارآمد یا هیچ فروپاشی شخصیتی فردی وجود ندارد که مدل یونانی یا رومی برای آن وجود نداشته باشد. بی‌جهت نیست که نام شخصیت‌های تراژیک یونانی در نظریه‌های فروید ظاهر می‌شوند. زن بی‌عدالتی‌دیده که در اندوه و جنونش خشن شده است؟ آیا آینیاس و دیدو را می‌خواهید یا جیسون و مدیا؟ و مانند هر دین اولیه خوبی، توضیحی برای پدیده‌های طبیعی داشتند، از تغییر فصل‌ها (دمتر و پرسفونه و هادس) تا اینکه چرا بلبل صدایش آنگونه است (فیلومنا و تریوس). خوشبختانه برای ما، بیشتر آن مکتوب شد، اغلب در چندین نسخه، تا به این ساختار روایی شگفت‌انگیز دسترسی داشته باشیم. و چون نویسندگان و خوانندگان دانش بخش بزرگی از این ساختار روایی، این اسطوره‌شناسی، را به اشتراک می‌گذارند، وقتی نویسندگان از آن استفاده می‌کنند، ما خوانندگان آن را تشخیص می‌دهیم، گاه به طور کامل، گاه فقط مبهم یا فقط به این دلیل که نسخه لونی تونز (Looney Tunes) را می‌شناسیم. این تشخیص تجربه ما از ادبیات را غنی‌تر، عمیق‌تر، معنادارتر می‌سازد، به‌طوری که داستان‌های مدرن خودمان نیز اهمیت می‌یابند و در قدرت اسطوره شریک می‌شوند.  

از میان جالب‌ترین تحولات اخیر در نوشتن برای خوانندگان جوان، مجموعه «پرسی جکسون و المپنشین‌ها» اثر ریک ریوردن است. پنج‌گانه رمان‌ها با «دزد صاعقه» (۲۰۰۵) آغاز می‌شود. پرسی نوجوانی است که نمی‌تواند جایی برای خود پیدا کند و می‌فهمد پسر پوزیدون است و متهم به دزدیدن سلاح برگزیده زئوس، صاعقه، شده است. سپس می‌فهمد دوستش ساتیر است، با مینوتور می‌جنگد، با دختری از آتنا دوست می‌شود، و همه جهنم به پا می‌شود. به عنوان یک نیمه‌خدا، پرسی با عادی‌بودن مشکل دارد (چیزهایی مانند ADHD و دیسلکسیا)، اما در جبهه قهرمانی واقعی است، همانطور که بارها و بارها فرصت اثباتش را می‌یابد. تبار الهی‌اش کمک می‌کند، همانطور که دوستان اسطوره‌ای‌اش. یک چیز است، می‌دانید، فرزند شاگرد ستاره‌دار سابق در مدرسه آمادگی جادوگری‌تان باشید، اما خدای دریا را پدر داشته باشید، خب...  

آه، فراموش کردم بگویم؟ آن عنوان والکات، «اومروس»؟ در گویش محلی، به معنای هومر است. طبیعتاً.

**The Lingering Shadow of the Sorrow King: Holden Caulfield’s Enduring Influence on Literary Disillusionment**  

J.D. Salinger’s *The Catcher in the Rye* (1951) irrevocably altered the literary landscape, introducing Holden Caulfield—a prototypical figure of adolescent disenchantment—whose raw emotionality, caustic worldview, and confessional narrative voice became a blueprint for subsequent authors. In the decades following the novel’s publication, writers have endeavored to replicate Holden’s essence, crafting protagonists who mirror his existential angst, confrontations with mortality, and fractured idealism. This emulation has spawned a subgenre of literature dominated by what might be termed “sorrow kings”: characters steeped in melancholic introspection, whose narratives dissect societal hypocrisy and personal trauma. Through works such as Stephen Chbosky’s *The Perks of Being a Wallflower* (1999) and Sylvia Plath’s *The Bell Jar* (1963), authors have channeled Holden’s legacy, weaving his thematic and stylistic DNA into their protagonists’ psyches, albeit with varying degrees of originality and depth.  

Chbosky’s Charlie, the introspective epistolary narrator of *The Perks of Being a Wallflower*, epitomizes this homage. Like Holden, Charlie is a social outsider whose laconic cynicism masks profound vulnerability. His letters—fraught with references to suicide, sexual awakening, and psychological trauma—echo Holden’s disjointed monologues, blending wry observation with visceral despair. Charlie’s fixation on his deceased friend Michael, whose suicide haunts the narrative, mirrors Holden’s obsession with his brother Allie’s death, underscoring a shared preoccupation with mortality as both a metaphysical quandary and a personal specter. Furthermore, Charlie’s navigation of adolescent sexuality—marked by awkward encounters and latent trauma—parallels Holden’s ambivalence toward intimacy, reflecting a broader critique of societal expectations. Chbosky’s deliberate invocation of Salinger’s voice, however, transcends mere imitation; it recontextualizes Holden’s disillusionment within the grunge-era 1990s, illustrating how existential disquiet persists across generations.  

Similarly, Sylvia Plath’s Esther Greenwood in *The Bell Jar* channels Holden’s caustic introspection, albeit through a distinctly gendered lens. Esther’s descent into mental illness—punctuated by suicide attempts, electroshock therapy, and a suffocating sense of societal entrapment—mirrors Holden’s psychological unraveling. Her scathing critiques of 1950s conformity (“I saw the years of my life spaced along a road in the form of telephone poles, threaded together by wires”) recall Holden’s diatribes against “phonies,” yet Plath amplifies the stakes by embedding Esther’s struggles within patriarchal constraints. Where Holden’s angst stems from a loss of innocence, Esther’s arises from the collision between intellectual ambition and rigid gender roles—a nuance that expands Salinger’s template. The Bell Jar’s clinical prose, interspersed with surreal imagery, diverges from Holden’s colloquial digressions, yet both narratives converge in their unflinching portrayal of protagonists teetering on the precipice of self-annihilation.  

The proliferation of such characters—including the unnamed narrator of *Catcher Caught* (a lesser-known but thematically resonant work)—reveals both the potency and limitations of Salinger’s influence. While these narratives adeptly replicate Holden’s voice and motifs, they risk eclipsing innovation with derivativeness. For instance, the tendency to conflate “depth” with references to suicide, sexual mishaps, or comas (as seen in the “catalogue” of tropes listed) occasionally reduces existential crises to aestheticized suffering. Yet, this trend also underscores a cultural truth: Holden’s enduring appeal lies in his embodiment of universal adolescent turbulence, refracted through a uniquely American lens.  

Ultimately, the sorrow king archetype persists not merely as a literary trope but as a mirror to societal anxieties. By grafting Holden’s essence onto new contexts, authors like Chbosky and Plath illuminate the timelessness of his struggle—even as they navigate the fine line between tribute and pastiche. Their works affirm that Holden Caulfield’s voice, though rooted in post-war America, continues to articulate the inarticulable sorrow of successive generations, ensuring his reign as literature’s perennial prince of disenchantment.

At the controls stands JOYCE GRENFELL, the 1st Traveller, with a look of weary exasperation that belies her years, her hair tucked up in a sensible bun, and her apparel a cross between a governess and an explorer.

Three students — VIVIAN, a bright-eyed young woman played by Carol Ann Ford, and her two friends, a curious girl with an assertive gaze, and a lanky boy with a mop of hair and a questioning look — stand awkwardly nearby. TRAVELLER (interrupting sternly)

FEMALE STUDENT FRIEND

Vanished, you say? Oh, heavens.

MALE STUDENT FRIEND
This is... there’s no way... it’s bigger on the inside!

TRAVELLER (sighing)
Yes, yes. A spatial anomaly — but that's beside the point. You are? Names, please.

This is Anne and that's John. Miss Traveller, they're my friends from uni. They wouldn't have come if they didn't care.

TRAVELLER (softening ever so slightly)
Vivian, my dear, I am not an ogre. It's just... The Old Lady isn't accustomed to... unexpected guests. She can be quite temperamental.

TRAVELLER (with a brisk tone)

VIVIAN

You're going to see! It's incredible!

TRAVELLER (addressing all three)

The Old Lady steadies and a soft hum replaces the violent shaking. The Traveller turns her attention to the controls, fiddling with dials with a practiced hand.

With a final lever pulled, the machine lurches once more. A symphony of alien sounds envelope the room as they launch into the vortex, the adventure beginning anew.

The Traveller, an enigmatic figure leading them into the unknown, watches over her new companions as the Old Lady travels onwards through time and space.

- **Assessment**: Before prescribing, a thorough assessment is necessary to rule out other causes of his symptoms that might mimic IBS, such as electrolyte imbalances or medications that could contribute to his symptoms.

Given your patient's condition (hemodialysis-dependency), drug removal by dialysis, altered drug metabolism, and potential drug accumulation must be considered.

It’s crucial to closely monitor the patient for any side effects, efficacy of the treatment, and potential interactions with his other medications. Adjustments may be necessary based on his response and any changes in his hemodialysis regimen.

Given the complexity of managing a hemodialysis patient with IBS, collaboration with a multidisciplinary team including nephrologists, dietitians, and possibly a gastroenterologist is advised to ensure optimal care.

For specific medication dosages and further individualized treatment plans, always refer to updated clinical guidelines and consider consulting with specialists when necessary. The pharmacokinetic profile of each drug can significantly differ in patients with CKD and on dialysis, thus close monitoring for efficacy and toxicity is paramount.

prompt.content: why do diffusion models use classifier free guidance, why is it considered a hack, and what are some better alternatives

chosen:
### Why Diffusion Models Use Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG)
**Classifier-free guidance** is a technique used in diffusion models (e.g., DALL·E 2, Stable Diffusion) to **enhance control over generated outputs** (e.g., aligning images with text prompts) without relying on an external classifier. Here’s why it’s widely adopted:

1. **Stronger Prompt Adherence**:  
   CFG amplifies the influence of conditional inputs (e.g., text prompts) by comparing a **"conditional"** prediction (guided by the prompt) with an **"unconditional"** prediction (no prompt). The difference between these is scaled and added to the final output, making generations more faithful to the prompt.

2. **Avoids Classifier Limitations**:  
   Earlier methods like **classifier guidance** required training a separate classifier to steer diffusion. This was brittle—classifiers struggled with noisy data, added computational overhead, and limited flexibility for diverse conditions (e.g., complex text).

3. **Simplicity & Efficiency**:  
   CFG trains a **single model** to handle both conditional and unconditional` generation by randomly dropping prompts during training (e.g., 10–20% of the time). At inference, it combines both pathways, avoiding extra models or complex setups.

---

### Why Is CFG Considered a "Hack"?
Despite its effectiveness, CFG is often called a "hack" for these reasons:
1. **Distribution Mismatch**:  
   CFG artificially exaggerates the difference between conditional and unconditional outputs. This pushes samples away from the true data distribution, leading to artifacts (e.g., oversaturated colors, unrealistic details).

2. **Hyperparameter Sensitivity**:  
   The **guidance scale** (e.g., `scale=7.0` in Stable Diffusion) must be tuned carefully. High values improve prompt alignment but reduce diversity/image quality; low values weaken control.

3. **Theoretical Impropriety**:  
   CFG isn’t derived from probabilistic principles. It’s an empirical trick that "hijacks" the model’s training objective, making generations **less probabilistic** and more deterministic.

4. **Trade-Offs**:  
   It sacrifices sample diversity for controllability—a compromise not inherent to the diffusion process itself.

---

### Better Alternatives to CFG
While CFG remains popular, these alternatives aim for more principled control:

1. **Reinforcement Learning (RL) Fine-Tuning**:  
   - **How**: Use RL (e.g., PPO) to optimize diffusion model outputs for reward metrics (e.g., prompt-image alignment via CLIP).  
   - **Pros**: Directly optimizes for desired objectives; avoids distribution distortion.  
   - **Cons**: Computationally expensive; unstable training.  
   - **Example**: [DPOK](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.13301) integrates RL with diffusion.

2. **GAN-Based Steering**:  
   - **How**: Employ a GAN discriminator to guide diffusion sampling toward high-reward regions.  
   - **Pros**: Leverages adversarial training for finer control.  
   - **Cons**: Adds complexity; GAN training challenges remain.  
   - **Example**: [Guided-Diffusion+GAN hybrids](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.12647).

3. **Improved Sampling Techniques**:  
   - **Consistency Models**: Train models to map noise to data in fewer steps, reducing the need for guidance.  
   - **Rectified Flow**: Straightens sampling trajectories for more efficient/stable generation.  
   - **Pros**: Faster sampling; less guidance dependency.

4. **Architectural Enhancements**:  
   - **Cross-Attention Refinement**: Strengthen text-image alignment in the model architecture (e.g., deeper cross-attention layers).  
   - **Perceiver Resamplers**: Better compress conditional inputs (e.g., long text) for more precise control.

5. **Energy-Based Models (EBMs)**:  
   - **How**: Use EBMs to define a scoring function for desired attributes, guiding diffusion sampling.  
   - **Pros**: Theoretically grounded; flexible control.  
   - **Cons**: Sampling slow; training instability.

---

### Key Insight
CFG dominates because it’s **simple, effective, and lightweight**—but its empirical nature and trade-offs make it a pragmatic "hack." Alternatives like RL or architectural innovations offer more rigor but at higher computational cost. As diffusion models evolve, expect hybrid approaches (e.g., CFG + RL) to bridge practicality and theory. For now, CFG remains the go-to for most applications.

\]

Now, apply the chain rule:
\[
\frac{dy}{dx} = (10u^9 + 5u^4) \cdot (-6x) = -6x (10u^9 + 5u^4)

Simplify the expression:
\[

\]
\[

**MATTHEWS**

**ZOE**

**THOMPSON**

1. **Balloon Blues:** The weather balloon strains against its tethers, lifting the capsule... sideways. Zoe’s face presses against the window as she dangles at a 45-degree angle.

**ZOE (Over radio, fading):**

**THOMPSON**  
*(Salutes with his cigar)*  
"Godspeed, Captain. Try not to break the timeline *too* much."  

**JACK**  
*(Wipes brow)*  
"Well, General... we did it?"  

**THOMPSON**  
*(Pulls out a new cigar)*  
"Son, we didn’t just do it. We did it with *style*. Now, who’s up for explaining this to Washington?"

chosen:
Here's a Roblox Lua script that changes a block to blue when a player clicks on it. Place this script directly inside the block (Part) in Roblox Studio:

```lua
-- Get the block this script is in
local block = script.Parent

-- Create a ClickDetector and parent it to the block
local clickDetector = Instance.new("ClickDetector")
clickDetector.Parent = block

-- Function to change block color to blue
local function onClick()
    block.BrickColor = BrickColor.new("Bright blue")
    -- Optional: Add visual feedback
    block.Material = Enum.Material.Plastic
end

-- Connect the function to mouse clicks
clickDetector.MouseClick:Connect(onClick)
```

### Key Components:
1. **ClickDetector**: Required for click interaction detection
2. **BrickColor**: Uses Roblox's named color "Bright blue" (RGB: 0, 0.6, 1)
3. **Material Change**: Optional visual enhancement (sets to smooth plastic)

### Setup Instructions:
1. Insert a Part (block) in Roblox Studio
2. Insert this script as a child of the block
3. Playtest - clicking the block will turn it blue

### Alternative Color Methods:
```lua
-- Using Color3 (RGB 0-1):
block.Color = Color3.new(0, 0.6, 1)

-- Using RGB values (0-255):
block.Color = Color3.fromRGB(0, 153, 255)
```

This script works for both base parts and unions. The color change is server-authoritative and visible to all players. For client-side only effects, you'd need a LocalScript with visual effects.

Here's a **15-day intensive email marketing learning plan** covering core concepts, tools, and practical skills. Each day includes key topics, actionable tasks, and resources. Aim for 2-3 hours/day.

---

### **Day 1-2: Foundations & Strategy**
- **Topics**: 
  - What is email marketing? (Goals, benefits, ROI)
  - Email types (Newsletters, promotions, onboarding, transactional)
  - Building an email strategy (Audience, objectives, KPIs)
- **Tools**: 
  - Research: HubSpot Blog, Mailchimp Guides
- **Action**: 
  - Define your target audience & goals.
  - Analyze 3 brands’ email campaigns (e.g., Amazon, Spotify).

---

### **Day 3-4: List Building & Compliance**
- **Topics**: 
  - Lead generation (Opt-in forms, landing pages)
  - Permission-based marketing (GDPR, CAN-SPAM)
  - List hygiene (Segmentation basics)
- **Tools**: 
  - Mailchimp, Brevo (free tiers), OptinMonster
- **Action**: 
  - Create a lead magnet (e.g., PDF checklist).
  - Build a compliant signup form.

---

### **Day 5-6: Email Copywriting & Design**
- **Topics**: 
  - Writing compelling subject lines/preheaders
  - Email body structure (AIDA framework)
  - Mobile-friendly design (Simplicity, CTAs)
- **Tools**: 
  - Canva, Beefree.io (templates), Hemingway App
- **Action**: 
  - Write 3 subject lines for a fake product.
  - Design a newsletter in Canva.

---

### **Day 7: Automation & Workflows**
- **Topics**: 
  - Welcome sequences
  - Trigger-based emails (e.g., abandoned cart)
- **Tools**: 
  - Mailchimp Automations, Brevo Workflows
- **Action**: 
  - Map a 3-email welcome sequence.

---

### **Day 8: Segmentation & Personalization**
- **Topics**: 
  - Why segment? (Demographics, behavior)
  - Dynamic content
- **Tools**: 
  - Mailchimp segments, Brevo personalization tokens

  - Segment a sample list (e.g., by location/interest).

---

### **Day 9-10: Email Service Providers (ESPs)**

  - Comparing ESPs (Mailchimp vs. Brevo vs. Klaviyo)
  - List import/export

prompt.content: Write a Doctor Who story about the Game Station

chosen:
## The Game Station Gambit

The TARDIS materialized with its usual wheezing groan, not in the bustling corridors of Satellite Five, but directly onto the shimmering, chrome-plated stage of **The Big Brother Eye** – the flagship game show of the 200th Century’s most insidious entertainment hub: **The Game Station**.

"Right then, Rose Tyler," the Ninth Doctor announced, stepping out in his usual leather jacket and intense stare. "Satellite Five. Year 200,100. Humanity's news and entertainment beamed straight into every home. Supposedly." He sniffed the air, thick with ozone, cheap synth-perfume, and the faint, metallic tang of fear. "Smells like trouble."

Rose followed, wide-eyed. Giant holographic screens pulsed with flashing lights and screaming contestants. A chrome podium dominated the centre, where a terrified-looking man in a silver jumpsuit was strapped, electrodes pulsing on his temples. A smooth, unnervingly cheerful voice boomed from hidden speakers.

"*Contestant Zeta-7! You have FAILED the loyalty quotient! The audience has spoken!*" The voice belonged to **The Editor**, a man in an impossibly sharp suit materializing beside them, his smile as cold as deep space. "Ah! Unexpected guests! Welcome to the pinnacle of human achievement! I am the Editor. And you are... disrupting the broadcast."

"We're just passing through," the Doctor said, his eyes scanning the complex machinery humming beneath the stage. "Big fan of... whatever this is. Looks expensive. And pointy."

"*The Big Brother Eye*," the Editor purred. "Where humanity's basest instincts are harnessed for ratings! Fear, humiliation, blind obedience... it's *deliciously* efficient. Keeps the populace docile, focused on the next prize, the next elimination. No messy questions about *why* the Fourth Great and Bountiful Human Empire seems to be... stagnating."

Rose felt a chill. "You're controlling them? Brainwashing them with this... this rubbish?"

"*Influencing*, my dear. Refining. Filtering out inconvenient truths. Like the energy fluctuations in Sector Seven, or the strange disappearances near the lower maintenance decks." The Editor's smile didn't reach his eyes as he looked pointedly at the Doctor.

The Doctor's face hardened. "Energy fluctuations? Disappearances? Funny, that. Almost sounds like something trying to break *in*. Or break *out*." He whipped out his sonic screwdriver, aiming it subtly at the base of the podium. A low hum resonated, making the Editor flinch. "This whole station... it's not just broadcasting propaganda, is it? It's a *shield*. A big, noisy, distracting shield. Hiding something *elsewhere* on the station."

Suddenly, klaxons blared. The holographic screens flickered, replaced by static, then a harsh, grating voice cut through the noise, echoing with metallic hatred:

"**ALERT! ALERT! UNAUTHORIZED TEMPORAL SIGNATURE DETECTED! THE DOCTOR IS PRESENT! EXTERMINATE! EXTERMINATE!**"

Rose gasped. "Doctor... that voice..."

"Daleks," the Doctor breathed, his face grim. "Of course. The Game Station. The ultimate distraction. Keep humanity staring at the shiny screen while the Daleks build their army in the basement!" He spun to the Editor, who looked genuinely shocked and terrified for the first time. "Your 'employers'? The ones who gave you this shiny station and told you to keep everyone looking the other way? They're not human. They're *genocidal pepper pots*!"

Panic erupted. Contestants screamed. Production staff ran. The Editor stammered, "They... they promised order! Progress! They said they were benefactors!"

"They lied!" the Doctor roared, grabbing Rose's hand. "They always lie! Now, where are they? Sector Seven? Lower decks? Talk!"

Before the Editor could answer, a section of the stage floor irised open. Not Daleks, but sleek, silver maintenance drones emerged, their single red eyes glowing with new, malevolent purpose. "**BY ORDER OF THE DALEK EMPIRE. YOU WILL BE DELETED.**"

"Run!" The Doctor yelled, pulling Rose towards a service corridor as energy bolts sizzled past them, vaporizing a camera drone. They ducked behind a bank of flickering monitors.

"We need to defend ourselves!" Rose shouted over the din.

"Defend? Rose, we need to *expose*!" The Doctor grinned, a fierce, dangerous light in his eyes. He pointed his sonic at the main broadcast array control panel nearby. "This whole station is a transmitter, yeah? Broadcasting lies? Let's broadcast a *truth*!"

He sonicked the panel furiously. Sparks flew. On every screen across the Game Station, and presumably beaming down to Earth, the image of the rampaging drones, the terrified humans, and the Doctor's face replaced the game show feed.

"People of the Fourth Great and Bountiful Human Empire!" the Doctor bellowed into a dangling microphone. "Look up! See what's *really* happening on your precious Game Station! It's not entertainment! It's a cage! A distraction while the Daleks prepare to turn you all into dust! They're here! Right now! In Sector Seven! They think you're stupid! They think you're blind! **PROVE THEM WRONG!**"

A stunned silence fell, then a roar – not of fear, but of outrage – erupted from the crew and contestants who hadn't fled. They grabbed tools, camera poles, anything they could find, turning on the drones.

The Editor, cowering near his podium, looked at the screens, then at the Doctor. "You've doomed us all!"

"No," the Doctor said, grabbing a fallen fire extinguisher. "I've given you a choice. Fight or die cowering. Now, Rose! Sector Seven! Time to crash a Dalek recruitment drive!"

As they sprinted towards the service lifts, leaving the chaos of the studio behind, Rose managed a breathless grin. "Fish fingers and custard later?"

"Survive this," the Doctor shot back, a manic energy in his step, "and I'll buy you a whole vat of custard. Now, run! The Daleks hate custard... almost as much as they hate *me*!"

The Game Station was no longer just a den of manipulation; it had become the frontline in a battle for humanity's soul, broadcast live across the stars. And the Doctor, as always, was right in the thick of it.

The rain drummed a steady rhythm on the traditional tiled roof of Genji Shimada’s Kyoto retreat. Inside, the air was thick with the scent of incense and old wood. Genji knelt in seiza before a low table, polishing the gleaming edge of his wakizashi, the rhythmic scrape of stone on steel a counterpoint to the storm outside. His cybernetic senses registered the heavy, deliberate footsteps approaching the engawa porch long before the knock came – a solid, resonant *THUD-THUD-THUD* that vibrated the delicate shoji screens.

He rose smoothly, sliding the door open. Towering in the downpour, water cascading off her broad shoulders and soaking her pink hair plastered to her scalp, stood Aleksandra Zaryanova. Her usual imposing presence seemed… *strained*. Her massive frame was hunched, not with fatigue, but with a peculiar, unfamiliar tension. Rain dripped from her jawline as she met Genji’s glowing visor.

"Genji," her voice was Zarya's deep contralto, but the cadence was wrong. Too quick, too tight. "I... I have a problem. A *big* problem."

Genji tilted his head, his green optical sensors narrowing slightly. "Zarya. You are soaked. Come in. What troubles you?" He stepped aside.

Zarya ducked through the doorway, water pooling instantly on the polished floor. She didn't move further into the room, just stood dripping, wringing her massive hands – a gesture Genji had *never* seen the confident soldier make. Her eyes, usually sharp and focused intensity, darted around the room with nervous energy.

"It's... it's not just a problem, Genji," she stammered, the deep voice cracking slightly. "It's... *me*. I'm not... I'm not *her*." The words tumbled out in a rush.

Genji remained perfectly still, processing. "Not her? Explain."

The figure before him took a shuddering breath, puffing out Zarya's broad chest. "It's me, Genji! *Lena*! Tracer! I'm stuck... I'm stuck *in here*!" She slammed a fist against Zarya's own armored chest plate with a metallic clang, the force making the floorboards tremble. The wide-eyed panic on Zarya's face was utterly alien. "This isn't my body! This is Zarya's! And I don't know where *she* is!"

Silence stretched, broken only by the drumming rain and the hiss of Genji's internal systems. He studied the face before him. The features were Zarya's, but the expression – the wide, frantic eyes, the trembling lower lip, the way she shifted her weight from foot to foot – was pure Tracer. The dissonance was jarring.

"How?" Genji asked, his synthesized voice calm, cutting through Tracer's panic.

Tracer-in-Zarya's-body swallowed hard, the movement prominent in the thick neck. "Chrono accelerator," she whispered, the single phrase heavy with dread and explanation.

Understanding dawned on Genji. The unstable temporal device was the only thing capable of such a profound violation of physical law. "I see," he murmured. "And Zarya? Where is she likely to be?"

Before Tracer could answer, another set of footsteps approached the engawa – light, rapid, almost skittering, but landing with unnatural heaviness. Another knock, hesitant and clumsy.

Genji slid the screen open again.

Standing in the rain, soaked and shivering violently in Tracer's signature orange bomber jacket (which looked stretched to its limits), was Lena Oxton's body. But the posture was all wrong. Here's a **17+ Thomas & Friends parody transcript** dialing the "Short Stature, Tall Temper" premise to 11 with chaotic, irreverent humor. *Disclaimer: This is a crude parody – no actual sentient trains were harmed (just their dignity).*

---

**SCENE START**  
*Sodor Yard. THOMAS (tiny, bright blue, visibly vibrating with rage) puffs next to PERCY (green, nervously chewing imaginary nails). GORDON (huge, smug) looms over them.*

**GORDON**  
*(Condescendingly)*  
Well, if it isn’t the garden gnome and his emotional-support teakettle. Fetching my coal, are we? Try not to strain your *delicate* pistons.  

**THOMAS**  
*(Eyes narrow, whistle shrieking like a kettle on crack)*  
**OH, YOU DID *NOT* JUST CALL ME A GNOME, YOU OVERINFLATED BAG OF HOT AIR!** I’ll shunt your tender so far up your boiler, you’ll be coughing up coal for a week!  

**PERCY**  
*(Whispering, sweating oil)*  
Thomas, maybe… don’t? He’s *twelve times* your size. And he’s got that whole… *main character energy*.  

**THOMAS**  
**SIZE ISN’T EVERYTHING, PERCY!** I’ve got **RAGE! And tactical brilliance!** Watch this!  
*Thomas attempts a menacing wheelie. Tips over. Lands sideways. Whistle stuck blaring.*  

**GORDON**  
*(Chuckles, steam puffing like cigar smoke)*  
"Tactical brilliance"? You just failed at *existing vertically*. Sir Topham Hatt uses you as a paperweight.  

**THOMAS**  
*(Struggling upright, voice cracking with fury)*  
**I’M A MULTI-FACETED LOGISTICAL ASSET!** I could derail you into next Tuesday before breakfast! I’ve got connections! *Dangerous* connections!  

**PERCY**  
You mean… Duck?  

**THOMAS**  
**DUCK’S GOT A SIDE HUSTLE, PERCY!** He knows a seagull who knows a *very* angry badger! **IT’S ON, GORDON!**  

**SCENE CUT - THE WATER TOWER**  
*Thomas tries to block Gordon’s access to the water tower by parking diagonally across the tracks. Gordon sighs, rolls forward slowly, and gently nudges Thomas into a puddle of muddy water.*  

**GORDON**  
Bath time, pipsqueak. Try not to drown in 3 inches of water.  

**THOMAS**  
*(Spitting mud, wheels spinning wildly)*  
**I’LL END YOU! I’LL INVENT A TIME MACHINE JUST TO GO BACK AND UNINVENT YOUR FAT CONTROLLER!** YOUR FIREMAN USES YOUR FIREBOX AS A TOASTER!  

**WORKER 1**  
*(Watching, eating a sandwich)*  
Y’know, for a steam engine, he’s got the vibe of a chihuahua who just did 3 lines of coal dust.  

**WORKER 2**  
*(Nodding)*  
He’s like if a toaster oven had daddy issues.  

**SCENE CUT - THE DOCKS**  
*Thomas tries to prove his strength by pulling a heavy load. He’s hitched to a single, empty crate.*  

**THOMAS**  
*(Straining dramatically, whistle screaming)*  
**BEHOLD MY MIGHT! I AM TITAN! I AM—**  
*The crate falls off. Thomas shoots forward like a bullet, crashes into a pile of fish crates. Seagulls descend, cackling.*  

**SEAGULL**  
*(Mimicking Thomas)*  
**"I AM TITAN!"** *[poops on Thomas’ funnel]* **"I AM SEABIRD SNACK!"**  

**THOMAS**  
*(Covered in fish guts, trembling with cosmic fury)*  
**I WILL FLAY YOU ALIVE AND WEAR YOUR FEATHERS AS A HAT!** PERCY! **GET ME A NAPALM CANISTER!**  

**PERCY**  
We… we don’t have those. We have coal. And mild disapproval.  

**SCENE CUT - THE ROUNDHOUSE (LATE NIGHT)**  
*Thomas is ranting to a cracked mirror.*  

**THOMAS**  
*(Dramatic whisper)*  
They laugh… but *I see the truth*. Gordon? Overcompensating. Percy? Clinically anxious. Henry? Literally bricked himself that one time. **I AM THE ONLY SANE ONE!**  
*The mirror cracks further.*  
**EVEN THE GLASS KNOWS I’M RIGHT!**  

**FAT CONTROLLER**  
*(Sticking his head in, weary)*  
Thomas, it’s 3 AM. Why are you screaming at reflective surfaces?  

**THOMAS**  
**BECAUSE THEY UNDERSTAND ME, SIR!** Unlike *some* people! *[muttering]* Probably tall… probably wears lifts in his boots…  

**FAT CONTROLLER**  
*(Pulls out a flask)*  
…I regret buying this railway off eBay.  

**FINAL SCENE - THE MAIN LINE**  
*Gordon breaks down. Thomas zips past, cackling.*  

**THOMAS**  
**KARMA’S A B****, HUH, GORDON?** Need a tow? **TOO BAD!** Enjoy your *extended scenic view* of the ditch!  

**GORDON**  
*(Weakly)*  
Go boil your buffers, you aggressive teapot…  

**THOMAS**  
*(Pulling into the station, triumphant)*  
**WHO’S THE GNOME NOW, SUCKERS?!** VICTORY IS M—  
*He misjudges the platform, slams into a luggage cart. Suitcases explode. A pair of novelty giant underpants lands on his funnel.*  

**PERCY**  
*(Gently)*  
…Tactical brilliance?  

**THOMAS**  
*(Voice muffled by giant Y-fronts)*  
**I MEANT TO DO THAT! IT’S A STATEMENT! RESPECT MY AUTHORITAH!**  
*[Incoherent screaming continues as the credits roll]*  

**END SCENE**  

---

Here's a detailed overview of current Swiss support programs and subsidies for emergency/backup power systems, based on official sources in German/French and translated to English. All information is current (2023-2024) and sourced from federal/cantonal authorities. Key focus areas include **critical infrastructure resilience** and **renewable-based backup systems**.

---

### 1. **Federal Program: Emergency Power Reserves for Critical Infrastructure**  
   **Source:** Federal Office for National Economic Supply (BWL/OFAE)  
   **Last Updated:** March 2024  
   **Language Source:** [BWL Notstromreserven (German)](https://www.bwl.admin.ch/bwl/de/home/energie/notstrom.html)  
   **Details:**  
   - **Objective:** Ensures continuous operation of essential services (hospitals, data centers, food supply chains) during blackouts.  
   - **Subsidy Coverage:**  
     - Up to 50% of **maintenance costs** for certified emergency generators (diesel/battery).  
     - Partial funding for **fuel reserves** and **system testing** (max. CHF 15,000VA/year).  
   - **Eligibility:** Companies classified as "critical infrastructure" under the National Supply Act (e.g., health, logistics, telecom). Requires registration with BWL and compliance with ISO 8528 standards.  
   - **Application:** Submit via BWL's online portal with proof of operational necessity.  

---

### 2. **Cantonal Program: Zurich's Backup Power Subsidy (Solar + Storage)**  
   **Source:** Office for Waste, Water, Energy, and Air (AWEL), Canton Zurich  
   **Last Updated:** January 2024  
   **Language Source:** [AWEL Solarförderung (German)](https://www.awel.zh.ch/energie/foerderprogramme/solarstrom.html)  
   **Details:**  
   - **Objective:** Promotes renewable-based backup systems for businesses to enhance grid independence.  
   - **Subsidy Coverage:**  
     - CHF 250–500/kWh for **battery storage** coupled with solar panels.  
     - Bonus of CHF 1,000 for **island-mode capability** (self-sufficient operation during outages).  
     - Max. subsidy: CHF 50,000 per company.  
   - **Eligibility:** SMEs, industrial firms, and agricultural enterprises in Zurich. Systems must have ≥10 kWh storage and grid-disconnect functionality.  
   - **Application:** Directly through AWEL after system installation.  

---

### 3. **National Tax Deduction: Energy Resilience Investments**  
   **Source:** Swiss Federal Tax Administration (FTA)  
   **Last Updated:** Tax Year 2024  
   **Language Source:** [FTA Direktabzug (German)](https://www.estv.admin.ch/estv/de/home/direkte-bundessteuer/deductions-for-companies.html)  
   **Details:**  
   - **Objective:** Tax incentives for companies investing in emergency energy infrastructure.  
   - **Coverage:**  
     - **100% direct deduction** for investments in "emergency power systems" (generators, UPS, microgrids) under accelerated depreciation.  
     - Applies to systems ensuring ≥48 hours of autonomous operation.  
   - **Eligibility:** All profit-oriented businesses. Systems must be certified by Swiss Safety Standards (SEV/ETL).  
   - **Process:** Declare in annual tax filings with equipment invoices and technical specifications.  

---

### 4. **Special Case: Agriculture & Remote Businesses**  
   **Source:** Swiss Federal Office of Agriculture (BLW)  
   **Last Updated:** November 2023  
   **Language Source:** [BLW Energieeffizienz (German)](https://www.blw.admin.ch/blw/de/home/instrumente/direktzahlungen/beitraege-fuer-oekologische-leistungen.html)

     - Minimum 5 kWp solar capacity + 10 kWh storage.  
     - Must replace diesel generators.  
   - **Grant Cap:** CHF 20,000 per site.  

---

**Title: The Boy Who Lived Twice**  

---

**Prologue: The Shattered Illusion**  
In a dimly corner of St. Mungo’s Hospital, James Potter cradled his lifeless son. The *real* Harry had succumbed to a fever, his tiny body failing hours after Lily’s death. Desperate, James fled to a crumbling lab beneath the English countryside—a joint NERV-Amagi facility destroyed in a failed experiment. There, he found a silver-haired infant, Jin Kanzaki, crawling unscathed through debris. A blood adoption ritual—infused with Sirius Black’s essence—rewrote the child’s DNA. Memory charms wove a lie so deep even Dumbledore believed it: *Harry Potter* lived.  

---

**Chapter 1: The Angel’s Shield**  
For eleven years, “Harry” endured the Dursleys’ cruelty, unaware of the dormant power humming beneath his skin. On Halloween 1991, Voldemort’s Killing Curse struck—and *rebounded*. The boy’s Angelic AT Field, a prismatic barrier born of his hybrid nature, shattered the Dark Lord. Dumbledore’s twinkling gaze saw only Lily’s “love,” not the truth: Harry was no wizard. He was a weapon.  

At Hogwarts, the Sorting Hat screamed *“GRYTHERIN!”*—a side effect of Sirius’s blood. Harry’s first year ended with Quirrell’s ash-strewn corpse, but the Dursleys’ looming return gnawed at him. That night, he wished for *home*. Tokyo-3’s neon glare answered.  

---

**Chapter 2: The Crawler of Shinjuku**  
Tokyo-3’s underbelly became his classroom. Harry—now “Jin” in his mind—mastered alleyway brawls, his magic mistaken for superhuman reflexes. As the masked vigilante **Crawler**, he dismantled yakuza rings, his knuckles bloodied but resolve steeled. Yet shadows watched: Gendo Ikari, NERV’s cold-eyed director, recognized the boy shaped by PROJECT NET.  

Kidnapped, strapped into EVA-01’s cockpit, Harry fought Angels as “Shinji Ikari.” Dumbledore stormed Japan, demanding his pawn’s return, only to be crushed by Ramiel’s laser—a death that severed Harry’s magical tether. The scar faded. The Boy Who Lived died.  

---

**Chapter 3: ZET Awakens**  
Post-Angel War, Gendo’s coup failed. Harry fled NERV, returning to Tokyo-3’s streets. A burning apartment complex tested his limits: he saved a family, collapsing as flames licked his skin. Waking in Amagi General Hospital, he faced Mitsugai Amagi—the zaibatsu’s patriarch.  

“You are NET Unit 2.0,” Mitsugai rasped, unveiling PROJECT NET’s purpose: to create hybrids to slaughter **Players**, eldritch horrors beneath Tokyo. Harry’s body could morph into **ZET**, a monstrous Angel-human fusion. Reluctantly, he agreed to train, clashing with Mitsugai’s grandchildren: Konoha, whose gentle eyes hid a tactical genius, and Kouga, whose fiery resolve birthed the armored hero **Alphas**.  

---

**Chapter 4: Britain’s Fall**  
Across the world, Privet Drive’s wards crumbled. Petunia’s drunken confession—*“We hated him!”*—sparked a Muggle police raid. The *Daily Prophet* declared Harry dead; Lucius Malfoy, framed for Dumbledore’s demise, rotted in Azkaban. Magic faded into myth, surviving only in Muggle-born whispers.  

---

**Chapter 5: The Player’s Gambit**  
EVOL’s attack on the Amagi Conference Center forced Harry’s hand. Seiji Hayami, EVOL’s smirking leader, reveled in chaos until ZET’s claws tore through his mechs. Victory tasted hollow. Tokyo-3’s streets now a cage, Harry boarded a bus to Kuoh—a town unknowingly hosting devils, angels, and a certain red-haired heiress named Rias Gremory.  

---

**Epilogue: Sisters in the Storm**  
Rei Ayanami watched her brother leap from a skyscraper, his superhero landing cracking asphalt. Her once-blue hair now flowed pink, vectors humming—a Diclonius Queen reborn. “Foolish boy,” she murmured, recalling their NERV days. Yet his longing for normalcy baffled her.  

A ping from Koyumi Araragi—her only friend, now a vampire hunter—jolted her. Vectors reshaped her dress; teleportation whisked her away. As “Kaede” vanished, Harry boarded the Kyoto bus, unaware of the supernatural storm awaiting him… or the sister who’d kill to protect his fragile peace.  

---

The collapse of British magic contrasts with Tokyo-3’s hidden wars, while Kuoh teases crossovers with *Highschool DxD*’s devils. Key themes: identity, legacy, and the cost of survival.

A **53-tooth chainring** in track cycling is typically used in specific scenarios where a **high gear ratio** is advantageous, particularly for events requiring **sustained power output** or **high-speed efforts**. Here's a breakdown of its use and relevance:

---

### **Key Applications in Track Cycling**
1. **Sprint Events (e.g., Match Sprint, Keirin, Team Sprint)**  
   - A 53T chainring, paired with a **small rear cog** (e.g., 14T or 15T), creates a **stiff gear ratio** (e.g., 53x14 ≈ **101.5 gear inches**).  
   - This setup maximizes **top-end speed** for explosive efforts over short distances (e.g., 200m flying laps).  
   - Sprinters with exceptional leg strength and power benefit from the larger chainring, as it allows them to maintain momentum on steeply banked velodromes.

2. **Time Trials (e.g., Kilo, 500m TT)**  
   - A 53T chainring can help riders maintain a **high cadence** while generating maximum power over 30–60 seconds.  
   - Combined with a 14T or 15T cog, it balances acceleration and top speed for these fixed-distance efforts.

3. **Large Velodromes (e.g., 250m+ tracks)**  
   - On longer tracks with gentler banking, a 53T chainring helps riders carry speed through straights and manage momentum through turns.  
   - Less common on smaller, steeper tracks (e.g., 166m), where smaller chainrings (48T–52T) are preferred for quicker acceleration.

---

### **Why 53T?**
- **Gear Ratio Flexibility**: A 53T chainring allows riders to use a wider range of rear cogs (12T–18T) to fine-tune ratios for different events or conditions.  
- **Road-to-Track Crossover**: Some riders adapt road components (e.g., 53/39T cranksets) for training or hybrid setups, though pure track cranksets often use smaller, stiffer chainrings (48T–54T).  
- **Cadence Management**: A 53T chainring can help riders avoid "spinning out" (reaching max cadence) on fast tracks, especially in events like the **Team Pursuit** or **Madison**.

---

### **Tradeoffs**
- **Acceleration**: Larger chainrings require more force to accelerate, making them less ideal for **mass-start races** (e.g., Scratch Race) where rapid accelerations are critical.  
- **Cadence Demands**: A 53T chainring demands a **lower cadence** to maintain speed, which may not suit riders who prefer high spin rates.  
- **Track Specificity**: On smaller velodromes, a 53T chainring can feel overly stiff, leading to fatigue in technical races with frequent surges.

---

### **Typical Pairings**
| **Event**          | **Rear Cog** | **Gear Ratio** | **Gear Inches** (27" wheel) |
|---------------------|--------------|----------------|-----------------------------|
| Sprint/Kilometer    | 14T          | 53x14          | ~102.2"                     |
| Team Pursuit        | 15T          | 53x15          | ~95.4"                      |
| Training/Road Hybrid| 16T–18T      | 53x16–53x18    | ~89.4"–79.5"                |

---

### **When to Avoid a 53T**
- **Novice Riders**: Smaller chainrings (48T–50T) are better for learning cadence control and technique.  
- **Technical Tracks**: On tight, steep tracks (e.g., London’s 250m Lee Valley Velodrome), smaller gears (e.g., 50x15) improve handling.  
- **Endurance Events**: Races like the **Points Race** or **Madison** often favor slightly smaller ratios (e.g., 50x15) for versatility.

---

### **Final Note**  
While a 53T chainring is more common in **road cycling**, its use in track cycling is situational. Elite sprinters or riders on large, fast tracks may favor it, but most track athletes opt for **smaller, track-specific chainrings** (48T–52T) to balance power and agility. Fred and George Weasley, covered in a fine dusting of soot and glitter from a particularly explosive experiment involving Fainting Fancies and Peruvian Instant Darkness Powder, stumbled upon a small, inviting pond.

"Blimey, George, look at that!" Fred exclaimed, wiping a streak of grime across his freckled cheek. "Looks cleaner than Mum's good china after one of her Scourgify frenzies."

"Cleaner than Percy's conscience after he snitched on us for the Nose-Biting Teacups, you mean," George grinned, already pulling off his vibrant orange Chudley Cannons t-shirt. "Fancy a dip? Wash off the evidence before Mum catches wind... literally and figuratively."

"Genius, as always, brother mine," Fred agreed, shucking his own shirt. They worked with the swift efficiency of years of shared mischief, shedding trousers and underpants until they stood side-by-side, gloriously naked in the warm summer air.

Both twins possessed the wiry, athletic build of Quidditch players – lean muscle honed from years of flying and dodging Bludgers (and occasionally, their mother's rolling pin). Their shoulders were broad, arms defined, legs long and sturdy. A constellation of freckles danced across their pale skin, stark against the ginger hair that crowned their heads. As they turned towards the water, George gave Fred an exaggerated once-over.

"Merlin's baggy Y-fronts, Fred, when did you last see sunlight? You're glowing like a Lumos charm!"

"Pot calling the kettle pale, Georgie?" Fred retorted, slapping his own stomach. "We're like two matching sticks of Weasley ginger, slightly singed at the ends." He then turned, presenting his backside to the pond with a flourish. "Though I must say, these finely sculpted buttocks deserve recognition. Pure Weasley marble, wouldn't you agree?" He gave a little wiggle.

George mirrored the action, bending over slightly. "Undeniably! A pair of pale moons, ready to eclipse the sun with their magnificence! Mum would be so proud." He chuckled, the sound echoing slightly in the quiet clearing.

With identical whoops, they plunged into the cool, surprisingly clear water. The relief was instant. They splashed, dunked each other playfully, and scrubbed vigorously at the soot and glitter clinging to their skin and hair.

"Ahhh," Fred sighed, floating on his back. "This is the life. Better than a prefect's badge, eh?"

"Infinitely," George agreed, scooping water over his head. "Though I wouldn't say no to the badge if it meant access to the prefects' bathroom... imagine the prank potential in *those* bubbles." He paused, a thoughtful look crossing his face. "Speaking of relief... that Exploding Eel sandwich from lunch is making its presence known."

A mischievous glint appeared in Fred's eye. "Race you? On three?"

"Always," George grinned.

They treaded water, facing each other.
"One..."
"Two..."
"THREE!"

A moment of intense concentration, then two distinct, bubbling eruptions disturbed the water's surface behind each twin. The bubbles rose with surprising vigor, creating small, turbulent patches. Twin sighs of profound contentment followed.

"Ahhhhh," Fred exhaled, his face a picture of blissful release. "Like letting the air out of a Bludger-swollen Blast-Ended Skrewt."

"Pure, unadulterated relief," George agreed, stretching luxuriously, water sluicing off his lean torso. "A symphony in methane!"

They floated for a moment, enjoying the afterglow and the cool water. Then George frowned, peering behind Fred. "Blimey, Fred, look. Are those...?"

Fred turned. Behind them, near the spots where the bubbles had surfaced, several small, silvery fish were floating belly-up. They looked distinctly lifeless.

"Merlin's soggy socks!" Fred exclaimed, paddling closer. He poked one with a finger. It didn't flinch. "George... did we...?"

George swam over, inspecting the casualties. A slow, wide grin spread across his face, mirroring Fred's own dawning realization. "Freddie, my boy... I do believe our natural emissions possess a certain... *potency*."

"Fish-felling flatulence!" Fred declared, awe mixing with amusement in his voice. "We've discovered a new weapon! Silent, deadly, and environmentally... well, *lethally* aquatic!"

"Think Mum'll be impressed?" George asked, already scooping up two of the larger, unfortunate fish.

"Doubtful," Fred laughed, grabbing two more. "But *we* are! Free dinner, courtesy of the Weasley Wind Company!"

Chortling, they waded back to the shore, clutching their unexpected bounty. They quickly dried off with a quick "Tergeo!" and dressed. Gathering dry twigs and branches, they soon had a small, crackling campfire going on the bank.

Skewering the fish on green sticks, they held them over the flames. The smell of cooking fish soon mingled with the scent of woodsmoke and the lingering dampness from the pond.

"To our fallen foes," Fred toasted, holding his sizzling fish aloft. "May their sacrifice fuel our next great prank."

"To biological warfare," George added, taking a tentative bite. "Huh. Not bad. Needs a bit of salt, maybe a hint of dragon's breath for authenticity."

"Next time, Georgie," Fred said, his mouth full. "Next time. Pass me that stick, I think this one's done. Smells better than it did ten minutes ago, that's for sure."

As they ate their "fart-grilled" fish by the fire, the twins plotted their next move, the pond glimmering behind them, blissfully unaware of the deadly digestive forces that had briefly invaded its depths. The only evidence was the satisfied smacks of the Weasley twins enjoying their uniquely acquired supper.

**Title:** **The Night Kirby Lit Up Zootopia**

The rain in Sahara Square wasn't the refreshing mist from the climate walls; it was a cold, persistent drizzle that slicked the sand into mud. In Tundratown, the heaters flickered erratically, leaving arctic foxes shivering in their own neighborhood. Over in Savanna Central, the power blinked out during rush hour, snarling the Monorail and leaving commuters like Officer Judy Hopps stranded for hours after a long, frustrating shift chasing a notoriously slippery pickpocket who got away. Nick Wilde’s carefully negotiated deal for a prime Pawpsicle stand location had collapsed spectacularly, leaving him dejectedly wiping blueberry stains off his best (only) tie. Even the usually cheerful sloths at the DMV seemed to sigh in slow motion.

Zootopia wasn’t just having a bad day; it felt like the entire city had collectively stubbed its toe, spilled its coffee, and missed the bus – all at once. A heavy blanket of gloom settled over the districts, muting the usual vibrant energy. Lights seemed dimmer, laughter was scarce, and shoulders slumped everywhere you looked.

Far, far away, on a star brighter than most, a certain round, pink hero felt a subtle shift in the cosmic mood. Kirby, ever attuned to the emotional wavelengths of the universe, perked up. Through his unique connection to all things joyful, he sensed a profound sadness radiating from a distant, diverse city. A city of animals, big and small, feeling utterly defeated. His big, round eyes widened with concern. *"Poyo?"* (Translation: "Oh dear, that won't do at all!")

Without hesitation, Kirby inhaled deeply, puffing himself up like a living balloon. With a determined *"Hiiiiii!"*, he launched himself into the starry void, riding his signature Warp Star. It streaked across galaxies, a comet of pure positivity, heading straight for Zootopia.

He landed with a soft *poof* in the darkened, rain-slicked plaza near the Zootopia Police Department headquarters. Judy Hopps, trudging out after her paperwork, nearly bumped into him. She blinked, her long ears drooping. "What in the...? A... pink ball?"

Kirby beamed up at her, his smile wide and impossibly bright. ***"Poyo!"*** (Translation: "Hello, sad bunny!") He did a little bounce, his round body jiggling adorably.

Judy, despite her exhaustion, felt a tiny spark of curiosity. "You're... not from around here, are you, little guy?"

Before she could react, Kirby inhaled sharply. Not to suck her up, but to draw in the cold, damp air around him. He puffed up even bigger, then exhaled a warm, gentle breeze that smelled faintly of strawberries and sunshine. The drizzle around them *stopped*, forming a small, dry, perfectly circular patch. Judy gasped as the unexpected warmth touched her fur.

***"Wah!"*** Kirby chirped, then began to float. He drifted gently upwards, his simple presence radiating an aura of pure, uncomplicated happiness. He started humming – a soft, wordless melody that seemed to vibrate with pure joy. It wasn't loud, but it carried strangely well through the quiet night.

A family of weary otters shuffling by paused. The smallest pup pointed. "Mama! Look! A floating marshmallow!" Kirby turned, spotted them, and did a playful mid-air somersault. ***"Hiiii!"*** The pup giggled, a sound that cut through the silence like a bell. The parents managed tired smiles.

Word spread. Lights flickered on in windows. Heads poked out of burrows and dens. A group of downcast elephants lumbering home from a cancelled show saw Kirby gently land on the head of the smallest calf. He bounced softly, making the calf trumpet with surprised delight. Kirby inhaled playfully near a discarded trumpet case left by a disheartened street musician, and suddenly *he* was holding a tiny, pink version of the instrument. He blew – not a perfect note, but a cheerful, kazoo-like *"Toot! Poyo!"* that made the elephants chuckle, a deep, rumbling sound of returning mirth.

He floated into the dimly lit streets of Nocturnal District. Bats and owls, usually bustling, were listless. Kirby spotted Flash Slothmore, looking particularly glum after his car wouldn't start. With a determined puff*, Kirby inhaled a discarded "Slow-Mo" energy drink can (empty, thankfully). Instantly, Kirby *slowed down*. He drifted towards Flash in exaggerated, comically slow motion, mimicking the sloth's pace. He reached out a tiny pink nub... slowly... slowly... and booped Flash gently on the nose. ***"Poooo... yoooo..."*** Flash's eyes widened in surprise, then crinkled at the corners. A slow, wide smile spread across his face, followed by an even slower, genuine laugh. "Heh... heh... heh... that's...... good..."

The laughter was contagious. Animals started gathering, drawn by the strange pink visitor and the growing pockets of unexpected joy. Judy and Nick found themselves side-by-side in the crowd, their own troubles momentarily forgotten, watching the spectacle unfolded.

Kirby became a one-puffball parade. He inhaled a dropped lollipop and blew shimmering pink bubbles that tasted like cotton candy. He copied a street performer's juggling act (using three floating apples he'd inhaled), bouncing them with adorable clumsiness. He saw a group of sad beavers near a leaking dam model and inhaled the water spray, puffing himself into a perfect, temporary water balloon shape before gently releasing it back, fixing the leak. The beavers cheered.

Soon, the entire plaza was filled with animals laughing, smiling, and sharing stories of their bad days, now softened by the shared experience and Kirby's infectious cheer. Someone started playing music – real music, upbeat and lively. Others joined in, dancing clumsily or tapping their feet.

Kirby, hovering in the center, beamed. His job was done with simple tools: boundless cuteness, a willingness to help, and the power to turn sadness into smiles. He’d absorbed the city's gloom and transformed it with pure, pink joy.

As the first hints of dawn painted the sky, the Warp Star shimmered above. Kirby gave one last, big wave to the now-buzzing, smiling crowd. ***"Poyo! Bye-bye!"*** Judy and Nick waved back, standing together, their earlier frustrations a distant memory.

"Y'know, Carrots," Nick said, a genuine smile on his face as he watched Kirby zoom away, leaving a trail of stardust, "I still have blueberry on my tie, and you still didn't catch Weaselton... but somehow, it feels like tomorrow might just be okay."

Judy nodded, watching the last sparkle of the Warp Star vanish. "It's amazing what a little unexpected kindness... and a very round, very pink dose of cheer... can do for a city."
